analyst_view.overall: Third against fourth, separated by one point: Freiburg (22 points) have won five in a row in all competitions, the latest 1-0 at Elversberg, and Leipzig (21) beat Union 5-1 and Lens 3-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday. Leipzig are without Marc Guiu and Assan Ouédraogo, and Castello Lukeba has a bruised knee; the numbers count all three. Freiburg miss Florent Muslija (cruciate ligament, counted) and Berkay Yilmaz is reported suspended after a red card, a squad player the numbers don't list. Both sides are busy: Freiburg host Twente in the Conference League on Thursday evening, and Martin Demichelis says Leipzig will rotate as fatigue builds. No referee is named yet; nothing I found clearly moves the numbers, so I stay with them.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, high for this fixture because Leipzig have scored 21 in their last six, and they already add for Lukeba's absence (+6% to Freiburg). Freiburg play on Thursday and Leipzig plan rotation, which could take some sharpness off both attacks, but Freiburg's run has been built on tight wins rather than open games. Nothing clear either way, so I stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, fairly evenly split, and already count both sides' recent corner form. Freiburg's wide play through Beste and Scherhant and Leipzig's through Nusa and Raum is what the numbers have seen all season, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards and already add 8.5% for Freiburg's recent bookings (15 in six, Yilmaz's red among them) while trimming for Leipzig's calmer record. No referee is named yet and this is a top-four game rather than a grudge match, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots and already take a little off Freiburg and add to Leipzig for recent form. A short turnaround for Freiburg after Thursday's Conference League game and Leipzig's rotation could make it slightly scrappier, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target and already add 5% for Leipzig's sharp recent finishing (46 on target in six). Guiu's absence is in the numbers, and nothing new points either way, so I stay at 9.6.
